rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creation glorifies God, teaching that He alone rules the world and alone deserves human gratitude.
rows.anchor: everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies God and by this glorification teaches man that God alone is the sovereign of this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power over all things is manifest; He needs no help or partner in creating or governing the world.
rows.anchor: it is absolutely clear that He has power over all things. He is not dependent on anyone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God has accomplished everything independently, servants should trust and serve Him alone, without associating partners.
rows.anchor: He has accomplished everything on His own, and just as He did this in the past, He will continue to do it in the future as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also created humanity; unlike the rest of creation, people have freedom, so some choose disbelief and others belief.
rows.anchor: since the Almighty has blessed man with the freedom to exercise his will, some among them as a result have become disbelievers and others believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God observes and judges each person's deeds; treating belief and disbelief alike would contradict divine justice and wisdom.
rows.anchor: If He does not do this, it will only mean that belief and disbelief are equal in status in His eyes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation has a true purpose, which requires a final day when truth's defenders are rewarded and its opponents punished.
rows.anchor: This verse substantiates what has been stated earlier: the A lmighty has created this world with a true purpose

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's well-formed creation recalls the Qur'anic description of people as fashioned in the finest mould.
rows.anchor: Everyone can see that man has been created in the best of moulds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings stand at creation's summit, with other creatures made to serve them directly or indirectly.
rows.anchor: He stands at the pinnacle and the summit of all other creatures, which have been created to serve him directly or indirectly

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's carefully fashioned inner and outer capacities show that worldly pleasure cannot be life's sole purpose; people must answer for their gifts.
rows.anchor: all this elaborate arrangement providence has made in his creation and in sustaining him will be rendered meaningless

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human formation, provision, and elevated status require that humanity be held accountable before its Lord.
rows.anchor: fashioning man in the best of forms, provision of apt sustenance and his high status among other creatures, require that he be held accountable before his Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an warns the deluded person that God perfected his form and arranged him as He pleased.
rows.anchor: people who are not convinced of the Hereafter and the reward and punishment which is going to take place in it are threatened thus

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God is necessary: otherwise, the world's purposeful creation and careful formation of humanity would be meaningless.
rows.anchor: the God who has created this world with a great purpose and has created man in such a diligent and elaborate manner, shows that he shall necessarily be returned to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything in the heavens and earth, including what people conceal or reveal; this knowledge grounds accountability and recompense.
rows.anchor: God is aware of all that is happening openly or secretly in this world and that this information will become a source of accountability for man

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier disbelieving nations, including ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Lot's people, suffered worldly punishment and face grievous punishment in the Hereafter; Quraysh knew their ruined settlements.
rows.anchor: This is a reference to the nations of ‘ Ād and Thamūd

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those histories show that God sends messengers and punishes their rejecters; Quraysh should therefore accept the coming universal day of justice.
rows.anchor: when people denied these messengers, they were severely punished by Him. The implication of the verse is that when the Quraysh are able to witness these examples

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past nations rejected messengers despite clear signs, arrogantly objecting that ordinary human beings could not be divinely appointed guides.
rows.anchor: these nations denied them because of arrogance and haughtiness and made up false excuses such as: asking why the Almighty made human beings His messengers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By these objections the nations rejected their messengers and their call to truth, so God left them to face the consequences.
rows.anchor: by making such objections and excuses, these people rejected their messenger and his calls to the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God arranges guidance for people's benefit, but does not force it on those who fail to value it; He is self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: if the Almighty wants to guide people it is not because this is something which is to His benefit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers who deny resurrection give no weight to the prophets' call.
rows.anchor: Since these disbelievers claim that

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to answer their unsupported denial emphatically under oath; its force answers one claim with another.
rows.anchor: the element of reasoning is stifled, and what is said is a claim in response to a claim because the latter claim has no reasoning behind it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine providence requires that the righteous and wrongdoers not be treated alike, so resurrection and judgment must occur.
rows.anchor: magnificence of which is evident in every speck of this universe, necessitates that He does not deal in the same manner with the righteous and the wrong-doers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is easy for God, whose knowledge and power are unlimited, unlike human beings with limited capacities.
rows.anchor: it is very easy for God; He has unlimited power and knowledge

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse admonishes disbelievers to profess faith in God's Prophet and in the Qur'an, the revealed light that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: The “light” obviously refers to the Qur’ ān revealed by Him to distinguish between the truth and untruth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book abandoned earlier revelation, while some later tried to extinguish the Qur'anic light, though God will perfect it.
rows.anchor: they seek to extinguish the light of God with blows [of air] of their mouths; but God has decided that He will perfect His light

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not imagine that God is unaware of their deeds, since they will answer for them.
rows.anchor: Each and everything they do is in His knowledge, and one day they will have to answer for all this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering is certain under God's scheme, supported by signs within and around humanity and by the testimony of prophets, messengers, and scriptures.
rows.anchor: Its advent is necessary to prove that this world is a meaningful creation, and if it does not come, then it would mean that this world is a purposeless creation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The references to assembling all people on one appointed day refute doubts that anyone could gather the countless inhabitants of land and sea.
rows.anchor: The stress in these verses of gathering all mankind on one day is to remove the doubt in the minds of these people that such an event is improbable

rows.speaker: Shāh ‘Abd al-Qādir
rows.claim: Shāh ʿAbd al-Qādir translates yawm al-tagābun as the day of victory and defeat; Islahi calls this translation very accurate.
rows.anchor: translated by Shā h ‘Abd al-Q ādir as “the day of victory and defeat.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains victory and defeat through the final outcomes: believers are forgiven and enter eternal gardens, while deniers enter Hell forever.
rows.anchor: those who embrace faith and do righteous deeds will be cleansed of the effects of their sins by the Almighty and admitted into gardens

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrongly treat worldly luxury or deprivation as victory or defeat; this world is a trial, and true victors are faithful doers of good in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: this world is not a place of reward; it is a place of trial. The Hereafter is the place of reward where only they will be the victors

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hereafter's victory belongs to faithful people who did good even if they had little worldly provision; those who lacked faith lose even if affluent.
rows.anchor: they were very affluent in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who see worldly life as success fear future need and hesitate to sacrifice; those oriented to the Hereafter spend for its lasting success.
rows.anchor: people who regard this world to be the place of success and failure, to help and serve others by sacrificing their own comforts and luxuries

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardship comes only by God's permission; obedience will not expose a believer to a trial beyond the capacity God knows in His servants.
rows.anchor: whatever he does while obeying the Almighty will never become for him a source of trial that is beyond his capacity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A steadfast believer's heart receives timely guidance through the Holy Spirit, and God's help arrives by means unseen to people.
rows.anchor: through the Holy Spirit will guide his heart at the right time. He is aware of everything and knows what befalls His servants

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus told his students not to worry about their defense because the Holy Spirit would teach them what to say.
rows.anchor: This is precisely what Jesus (sws) had told his students: “Do not worry about how you will defend yourselves or what you will say

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh should not evade obedience through false notions; the Prophet's task is only to communicate God's guidance clearly, and hearers answer for rejecting it.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) will not be asked about their faith; it is they themselves who will be asked why they did not accept his call

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God can bring harm or benefit, so believers should place their trust in Him; this follows from their faith.
rows.anchor: There is no other deity in the heavens and in the earth from whom one can fear any harm or expect any benefit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of wife and children can test believers when it conflicts with devotion to God and blocks duties involving life and wealth.
rows.anchor: there is a possibility that he will be so overcome by the love and interest of his wife and children that he will end up ignoring his love for God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some families become enemies in effect by obstructing duties to God, even when their interference comes from good intentions.
rows.anchor: They are instrumental in stopping a person from fulfilling his duties towards God. Although this attitude emanates from them as well-wishers of that person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer should guard against family obstructing God's cause while preserving ties as far as possible and forgiving relatives.
rows.anchor: At the same time, this should not lead him – as far as is possible for him – to sever his relations with them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guard against family pressure while trying to reform relatives and forgiving them; maintain relations unless they commit disbelief.
rows.anchor: He must not sever his relationship with them, unless they commit some act of disbelief, and should keep forgiving them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children test whether people become infatuated with them or use them to seek God's love and pleasure; the latter path brings success.
rows.anchor: The Almighty tries a person through his wealth and children. He judges whether he forgets Him by being infatuated by these or makes them a means to earn His love and pleasure

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should love God most; even worldly losses from choosing this path will be compensated by great reward in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: in the Hereafter the Almighty will compensate every loss with great reward

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending for God is the remedy for greed's domination; weaken it until it can no longer impede virtuous deeds.
rows.anchor: he should weaken it by spending for the cause of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suppressing greed by God's blessing is the effort that makes a person worthy of success in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: succeed in this effort are worthy of success in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuḥḥ means greed and avarice; when this innate trait dominates a person, it leads to ruin, while those protected from it succeed in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: If this greed found innately in a person dominates him, then it will lead him to doom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because greed is an instinct of the soul, like sexual drive or anger, it must be checked before it defeats sacrifice and altruism; spending for God weakens it.
rows.anchor: this is among those instincts against which if a person does not remain on guard will lead him to doom the way sexual drive or anger can

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending despite personal need is especially praiseworthy and exemplified by believers preferring others over themselves.
rows.anchor: and they give preference to them over their own selves though they are in want

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After general spending, this verse specifies spending for jihad; Qur'anic references to giving God a loan indicate that special expenditure.
rows.anchor: In this verse, believers are specifically and emphatically urged to spend for jihād

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḍāʿafah means increase or multiplication, not only a doubling.
rows.anchor: does not merely mean “to be doubled:” it also means “to increase” whether this increase is of the nature of being doubled or of being multiplied many times

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's request for a loan does not reflect need; it gives people a chance to gain great returns, even tenfold or seventyfold.
rows.anchor: The purpose is to provide these people with an opportunity to earn great profit – as much as ten, in fact seventy times – by spending in His way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A goodly loan comes from pure wealth, given generously and willingly, even by someone in need; God multiplies its repayment and forgives the giver.
rows.anchor: It means that this loan should be given from good and pure wealth with generosity and with willingness of the heart

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shakūr describes God as one who appreciates and welcomes servants' good deeds, values their offerings, and increases their reward despite His self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: the Almighty greatly values the good deeds of His servants and greatly welcomes them, even though He is self-sufficient and praiseworthy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forbearance means He deals generously with servants and overlooks the faults of those who try to shield themselves from sin.
rows.anchor: If they try to shield themselves from sins, He ignores their faults and blemishes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sacrifice made to please God is hidden from Him; He is mighty and wise, so those who trust His guidance succeed.
rows.anchor: whatever sacrifice people will make to please Him will never be concealed from His eyes
